item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00443","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C18","C17","C20"],"selected_candidate_label":"C18","confidence":0.78,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C18 plausibly supplied material language and argumentative structure for the later Yugoslavia notification. Both texts connect aid under the Mutual Defense Assistance Program to the security of the North Atlantic area, invoke consultation with North Atlantic Treaty governments, and move from an urgent foreign-security predicate to the use of specified funds for immediate assistance. C17 supplies relevant statutory machinery but not the child's distinctive justificatory narrative, while C20 shares only the generic concept of an interim emergency measure.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Yugoslavia's ability to defend itself... will contribute to the preservation of the peace and security of the North Atlantic area. The governments of the other nations which are members of the North Atlantic Treaty have been consulted on this point.","parent_excerpt":"We have been consulting with our associates in the North Atlantic Treaty with a view to determining what additional resources must be used by them and by us to provide an adequate common defense.","explanation":"Both use consultation with North Atlantic Treaty partners as support for a defense-assistance decision."},{"child_excerpt":"It is a settled premise of our foreign policy that the peace and security of the North Atlantic area is vital to the security of the United States.","parent_excerpt":"It is estimated that $3,504,000,000 will be required for strengthening the security of the North Atlantic area. The security of this area is of paramount importance to the strength of the entire free world.","explanation":"The later letter closely reuses the proposition that North Atlantic-area security is independently vital and justifies American assistance."},{"child_excerpt":"I have determined that it is essential... to use not to exceed $16 million of the funds appropriated for the purposes of Title I of the Act to provide food for Yugoslavia... This use of these funds is part of the interim aid program to meet the immediate emergency","parent_excerpt":"For this reason, I recommend that the Congress provide $4,000,000,000 in additional funds, to be used under the Mutual Defense Assistance Program.","explanation":"Both culminate the security rationale in a quantified funding action under the same assistance program, although the child adapts the machinery from an appropriation request to a statutory notification of fund use."}]}
